title: How a Diesel Engine Works in 60 Seconds 🚛🔥 #shorts
description:
A diesel engine has no spark plugs. It squeezes air so hard that the air gets hot enough to ignite fuel on its own, the instant fuel is sprayed in. That high compression is also why diesels are more efficient than gasoline engines. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#dieselengine #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A diesel engine has *no spark plugs*. It lights its fuel with hot air alone.

steps.label: Intake
steps.text: First the piston moves down and pulls in *fresh air*. Just air, no fuel.

steps.label: Squeeze
steps.text: Then it squeezes that air into a tiny space, often *16 to 20 times* smaller.

steps.label: Heat
steps.text: Squeezed air gets *hot*, around 500 degrees Celsius. Hot enough to ignite diesel.

steps.label: Injection
steps.text: An *injector* sprays fuel in, and it explodes instantly, slamming the piston down.

steps.label: Exhaust
steps.text: Finally the piston rises and pushes the *exhaust* out. Then it all repeats.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Squeeze, heat, *ignite*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
